|title='The Morning Show' & 'Succession' Lead Critics Choice Awards TV Nominations |last=Pedersen |first=Erik |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=December 5, 2023 |access-date=December 5, 2023}} The film nominations were announced on December 13, 2023.{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2023/12/critics-choice-film-nominations-2023-1235665954/ |title=The Critics Choice is 'Barbie' with 18 CCA Nominations; 'Oppenheimer', 'Poor Things' Follow with 13 Each |last=Hammond |first=Pete |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=December 13, 2023 |access-date=December 13, 2023}} The ceremony was originally due to take place at the [[Fairmont Century Plaza]], the Critics Choice Awards' home base which the [[Critics Choice Association]] (CCA) helped re-open in 2022, but was later moved to [[Santa Monica, California|Santa Monica]]'s [[Santa Monica Airport#Barker Hangar|Barker Hangar]], due to a [[labor dispute]] at the Fairmont Century Plaza. ''[[Barbie (film)|Barbie]]'' led the film nominations with a record-breaking eighteen, followed by ''[[Oppenheimer (film)|Oppenheimer]]'' and ''[[Poor Things (film)|Poor Things]]'' with thirteen each. ''[[The Morning Show (American TV series)|The Morning Show]]'' led the television nominations with six, followed by ''[[Succession (TV series)|Succession]]'' with five. Additionally, the cultural phenomenon of "[[Barbenheimer]]" received a total of 31 nominations, winning fourteen: 8 for ''Oppenheimer'' and 6 for ''Barbie''.{{cite web |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/siladityaray/2024/01/15/critics-choice-awards-barbenheimer-win-big-once-again-as-harrison-ford-delivers-nights-most-memorable-speech/ |title='Barbie' and 'Oppenheimer' Dominate Critics Choice Awards |last=Ray |first=Siladitya |work=[[Forbes]] |date=January 15, 2024 |access-date=January 15, 2024}} Overall, [[Warner Bros. Pictures]] received a total of 25 nominations for film, the most for any studio this year; [[HBO]] / [[HBO Max|Max]] received a total of 23 nominations for television, the most for any network this
